bib.title: Reading Wikipedia to Answer Open-Domain Questions

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Reading Wikipedia to Answer Open-Domain Questions" (DrQA). Danqi Chen, Adam Fisch, Jason Weston, Antoine Bordes. ACL 2017, pages 1870–1879, doi 10.18653/v1/P17-1171. The PDF is the ACL proceedings version, not the arXiv 1704.00051 preprint. Its page numbers 1870–1879 match PDF pages 1–10.

COVERAGE: I read all 40,612 extracted characters across all 10 pages, including the references. I skipped nothing.

CLAIMS (ranked)

- claim: DrQA has two parts. A Document Retriever that does not use machine learning, and a neural Document Reader that pulls out answer spans. This is the retrieve-then-read split the note refers to.
  number: none
  setup: open-domain QA with Wikipedia as the only knowledge source
  quote: "We develop DrQA, a strong system for question answering from Wikipedia composed of: (1) Document Retriever, a module using bigram hashing and TF-IDF matching designed to, given a question, efficiently return a subset of relevant articles and (2) Document Reader, a multi-layer recurrent neural network machine comprehension model trained to detect answer spans in those few returned documents."
  where: p2 (1871)

- claim: The retriever scores TF-IDF bag-of-words vectors. It adds hashed bigram features and returns the top 5 articles to the reader.
  number: 2^24 hash bins; top 5 articles
  setup: inverted index plus term-vector scoring, unsigned murmur3 hash, following Weinberger et al. 2009
  quote: "Our best performing system uses bigram counts while preserving speed and memory efficiency by using the hashing of (Weinberger et al., 2009) to map the bigrams to 224 bins with an unsigned murmur3 hash. We use Document Retriever as the first part of our full model, by setting it to return 5 Wikipedia articles given any question."
  where: p3–4 (1872–1873). The extraction shows "224"; it is the superscript 2^24.

- claim: The retriever beats the built-in Wikipedia Search on three of four datasets. Bigrams help most on WikiMovies and SQuAD, but on WebQuestions they do slightly worse than plain TF-IDF.
  number: answer appears in top-5 pages, Wiki Search / plain / +bigrams: SQuAD 62.7/76.1/77.8; CuratedTREC 81.0/85.2/86.0; WebQuestions 73.7/75.5/74.4; WikiMovies 61.7/54.4/70.3
  setup: 2016-12-21 English Wikipedia dump, 5,075,182 articles. Metric is the % of questions for which an answer string appears in at least one of the top 5 pages. This measures string presence, not whether the passage is relevant.
  quote: "SQuAD 62.7 76.1 77.8 / CuratedTREC 81.0 85.2 86.0 / WebQuestions 73.7 75.5 74.4 / WikiMovies 61.7 54.4 70.3 ... Table 3: Document retrieval results. % of questions for which the answer segment appears in one of the top 5 pages returned by the method."
  where: p6 (1875), Table 3

- claim: Okapi BM25 and bag-of-embeddings cosine retrieval did worse than TF-IDF with bigrams. The paper gives no numbers for either.
  number: none
  setup: same retrieval task as Table 3
  quote: "We also compare doing retrieval with Okapi BM25 or by using cosine distance in the word embeddings space (by encoding questions and articles as bag-of-embeddings), both of which we find performed worse."
  where: p7 (1876)

- claim: Given the gold paragraph, the reader alone was state of the art among published single models on SQuAD. R-net, listed only from the leaderboard, scored higher.
  number: test 70.0 EM / 79.0 F1; dev 69.5 EM / 78.8 F1; R-net test 71.3 / 79.7
  setup: SQuAD v1.1, single model, 3-layer BiLSTM with h=128, 300-d GloVe, Adamax, dropout 0.3
  quote: "Our system (single model) can achieve 70.0% exact match and 79.0% F1 scores on the test set, which surpasses all the published results and can match the top performance on the SQuAD leaderboard at the time of writing."
  where: p7 (1876); Table 4, p8 (1877)

- claim: When the reader has to search all of Wikipedia instead of being handed the paragraph, SQuAD EM falls by more than half. Even with the correct document it reaches only 49.4.
  number: 69.5 to 27.1 EM; 49.4 given the correct document
  setup: SQuAD dev questions, full Wikipedia, SQuAD-trained reader
  quote: "DrQA's performance on SQuAD compared to its Document Reader component on machine comprehension in Table 4 shows a large drop (from 69.5 to 27.1) as we now are given Wikipedia to read, not a single paragraph. Given the correct document (but not the paragraph) we can achieve 49.4, indicating many false positives come from highly topical sentences. This is despite the fact that the Document Retriever works relatively well (77.8% of the time retrieving the answer, see Table 3)."
  where: p8 (1877)

- claim: Full-system open-domain EM is modest. Distant supervision raises it on every dataset, and the multitask model is best on three of four. On CuratedTREC, per-dataset fine-tuning (25.7) edges out multitask (25.4).
  number: top-1 EM, SQuAD-only / +Fine-tune(DS) / +Multitask(DS): SQuAD 27.1/28.4/29.8; CuratedTREC 19.7/25.7/25.4; WebQuestions 11.8/19.5/20.7; WikiMovies 24.5/34.3/36.5
  setup: full Wikipedia, retriever fixed. Streamlined reader without CoreNLP token features or lemmas. WebQ and WikiMovies answers restricted to candidate lists (1.6M Freebase entity strings for WebQ).
  quote: "SQuAD (All Wikipedia) n/a 27.1 28.4 29.8 / CuratedTREC 31.3 19.7 25.7 25.4 / WebQuestions 39.8 11.8 19.5 20.7 / WikiMovies n/a 24.5 34.3 36.5 / Table 6: Full Wikipedia results. Top-1 exact-match accuracy (in %, using SQuAD eval script)."
  where: p9 (1878), Table 6

- claim: The authors credit most of the gain to extra in-domain data, not to task transfer.
  number: none
  setup: Table 6 comparison
  quote: "The majority of the improvement from SQuAD to Multitask (DS) however is likely not from task transfer as fine-tuning on each dataset alone using DS also gives improvements, showing that is is the introduction of extra data in the same domain that helps."
  where: p8 (1877)

- claim: DrQA, using Wikipedia only, scores below YodaQA, which draws on several sources including Freebase and DBpedia.
  number: CuratedTREC 25.4 vs 31.3; WebQuestions 20.7 vs 39.8
  setup: YodaQA numbers are copied from its GitHub benchmarks page, not rerun
  quote: "it is reassuring that our performance is not too far behind on CuratedTREC (31.3 vs. 25.4)."
  where: p8 (1877)

- claim: Distant supervision builds training data from question–answer pairs alone. It retrieves the top 5 articles, keeps paragraphs that contain the exact answer, filters them, and scores answer positions by n-gram overlap with the question.
  number: paragraphs 25–1500 chars; 20-token window; up to 5 paragraphs. DS training sizes: SQuAD 71,231; TREC 3,464; WebQ 4,602; WikiMovies 36,301
  setup: Section 4.4, following Mintz et al. 2009
  quote: "All paragraphs shorter than 25 or longer than 1500 characters are also filtered out. ... we score all positions that match an answer using unigram and bigram overlap between the question and a 20 token window, keeping up to the top 5 paragraphs with the highest overlaps."
  where: p6 (1875)

- claim: The reader depends on exact-match and aligned-attention features. Removing both drops F1 by 19.4 points.
  number: 78.8 to 59.4 F1
  setup: SQuAD dev, ablation
  quote: "No faligned and fexact match 59.4 (-19.4)"
  where: p8 (1877), Table 5

- claim: The approach is generic and does not depend on Wikipedia's link structure.
  number: none
  setup: design statement
  quote: "our approach is generic and could be switched to other collections of documents, books, or even daily updated newspapers."
  where: p1 (1870)

LIMITS:
- The paper reports no test of any other corpus. The genericity claim is asserted, not measured.
- The retriever and reader are trained separately. The authors name end-to-end training as future work: "perform end-to-end training across the Document Retriever and Document Reader pipeline, rather than independent systems" (p9). The reader also trains on paragraphs independently, not across documents.
- Retrieval recall counts any answer-string occurrence in the top 5. It is not a relevance judgement.
- The BM25 and embedding comparisons give no numbers.
- The authors concede that much of the SQuAD drop comes from SQuAD questions being ambiguous out of context: "Additional resources other than SQuAD, specifically designed for MRS, might be needed to go further" (p8).
- Results are a single run with no variance reported.
- The paper is dated: an LSTM extractive reader, top-1 EM of 20–37%, pre-BERT and pre-dense retrieval. The generator in the note's sense is an extractive span classifier here. It does not generate text.
- The note calls it a "document reader" and a "Wikipedia retriever". The paper's own terms are "Document Retriever" and "Document Reader", and it names the setting "machine reading at scale (MRS)".

BUILDS ON (as printed): TF-IDF and bigram feature hashing (Weinberger et al., 2009); the Elasticsearch-based Wikipedia Search baseline (Gormley and Tong, 2015); AttentiveReader (Hermann et al., 2015; Chen et al., 2016); aligned question embedding (Lee et al., 2016); GloVe (Pennington et al., 2014); distant supervision (Mintz et al., 2009); multitask learning (Caruana, 1998; Collobert and Weston, 2008); SQuAD (Rajpurkar et al., 2016); CuratedTREC and YodaQA (Baudiš and Šedivý, 2015; Baudiš, 2015); WebQuestions (Berant et al., 2013); WikiMovies (Miller et al., 2016); earlier pipeline QA systems DeepQA (Ferrucci et al., 2010) and AskMSR (Brill et al., 2002).

CODE: none. The paper contains no code. The useful method lines are the reader's span scoring, P_start(i) ∝ exp(p_i W_s q) and P_end(i) ∝ exp(p_i W_e q), with i ≤ i′ ≤ i+15 (p4, 1873).

FIGURES: Figure 1, "An overview of our question answering system DrQA.", p3. It shows a question going into the Document Retriever over Wikipedia, then the Document Reader, then an answer ("833,500"), with the four evaluation datasets labelled. It is the cleanest diagram of retrieve-then-read for the "two components" section.

PROBLEMS:
- Superscripts were lost in extraction. "224 bins" is 2^24.
- The f_exact_match and f_aligned subscripts in Table 5 came out as plain text.
- The file is the ACL proceedings PDF, not the arXiv version named in the task. The content should be the same, but I did not compare them.
- The PDF contains no embedded instructions.
